high.title: Latest Savings Interest Rate Forecast After 30/4 Holiday
high.summary: Interest rates and tight liquidity conditions remain the biggest concerns discussed at bank annual general meetings in 2026. According to S&I Credit Rating Company's latest banking sector performance report, despite expectations that deposit interest rates would cool down after the State Bank Governor's meeting with banks in early April 2026, mobilization pressure persists, making the possibility of significant short-term rate cuts limited. VPBank's CEO Nguyen Duc Vinh explained that high deposit rates in Q1/2026 were mainly due to relatively tight market liquidity and high credit growth. New regulations also contributed to this trend. This signals continued pressure on VND funding costs, which directly impacts lending rates and overall monetary conditions. For FX and bond traders, sustained high rates could support VND stability but may pressure economic growth and corporate borrowing costs.

high.title: Savings Interest Rates May 2026: Cooling Across the Board
high.summary: Vietnamese banks have broadly adjusted deposit interest rates in early May 2026, with changes ranging from 0.2-0.8% depending on tenure and institution. State-owned banks show notable moves: Vietcombank now quotes 3.5%/year for 6-9 month terms, 5.9%/year for 12 months, and 6.0%/year for 24+ months (their highest rate). BIDV mirrors these levels exactly. This coordinated reduction suggests SBV guidance is taking effect, potentially easing the liquidity pressure that drove rates higher in Q1/2026. For VND traders, lower deposit rates could signal reduced pressure on the currency from hot money flows, while bond investors should watch for potential yield compression as funding costs normalize. The move supports economic growth prospects but may indicate continued central bank vigilance on inflation.

high.title: "Money Mountain" at Banks Surges as Hoa Phat Bears 15 Billion VND Interest Daily
high.summary: Hoa Phat's Q1/2026 interest expense hit a record 1.333 trillion VND, averaging nearly 15 billion VND daily - double the 2024 level and 14% higher than Q4/2025. The company attributes this to discontinuing capitalization after Dung Quat 2 became operational and sustained high VND lending rates in Q1/2026. The supply-demand imbalance forced banks to raise deposit rates to attract funds for growing business credit demand, keeping lending rates elevated throughout Q1/2026. Hoa Phat's total financial debt stood at 90.617 trillion VND at Q1-end, slightly down from year-end's 92.174 trillion as loan repayments begin for Dung Quat 2 project. This corporate borrowing pressure exemplifies the tight credit conditions affecting major Vietnamese enterprises and suggests continued upward pressure on VND interest rates, which could support bond yields but challenge economic growth.

medium.title: 20 Biggest Profit Champions on Stock Exchange Q1/2026: 5 Companies Earn Over 10,000 Billion VND, Banks Dominate, Vinhomes Shocks
medium.summary: Q1/2026 showed significant improvement in listed company profits, with 5 companies earning over 10 trillion VND compared to only 2 in Q1/2025. Vinhomes led with 30.727 trillion VND pre-tax profit (700% growth), while major banks continued dominating the high-profit rankings, reflecting the strong performance of Vietnam's financial sector.

medium.title: World Gold Prices Suddenly Drop Sharply on May 1 Evening
medium.summary: International gold prices dropped to $4,561/ounce on May 1 evening, falling $70 from morning levels despite USD weakness. DXY Index broke below 98 points to 97.9 - lowest in 2 months. Oil prices also cooled to $110/barrel. Analysts cite Middle East conflict's oil supply shock driving inflation concerns and forcing central banks toward hawkish monetary policies.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Bar Prices Morning May 1
medium.summary: International gold opened at $4,624/ounce, up 0.05% as USD weakened and oil prices declined. Gold recovered 1.7% in previous session after hitting one-month lows. Weak USD makes gold more attractive for non-USD currency holders, while reduced oil prices ease inflation concerns that had pressured Fed rate cut expectations.

medium.title: 20 Securities Companies Report Losses in Q1/2026, One Records 200 Billion VND Loss
medium.summary: Twenty securities companies reported losses in Q1/2026, up from 13 in Q4/2025, reflecting market liquidity challenges and intensified competition. EVS Securities recorded the largest loss at 197 billion VND compared to 18 billion profit in Q1/2025. This indicates continued stress in Vietnam's securities industry amid subdued market activity.

medium.title: Naming 7 Banks Set to Establish in International Financial Center
medium.summary: Seven major Vietnamese banks received shareholder approval to establish 100% owned subsidiaries in the International Financial Center (VIFC): Vietcombank, HDBank, SHB, MB, TPBank, LPBank, and Nam A Bank. Most plan 3,000 billion VND charter capital, signaling major expansion into international financial services and deeper integration into regional financial value chains.
